name: lodash-maxby-iteratee-jop
behavioral_change: lodash v4.0.0 split the iteratee-accepting forms of `_.max` and `_.min` into `_.maxBy` and `_.minBy`; `_.max` and `_.min` no longer accept an iteratee and silently ignore the second argument, comparing elements directly. The same release also split `_.sample` with a count into `_.sampleSize`.
downstream_effect: The downstream project's operation table in lib/processor.js maps `min` and `max` directly to `_.min` and `_.max` and calls them with a compiled user expression as iteratee; after the upgrade the iteratee is ignored and the wrong object is returned (for example max age yields {name: Andrea, age: 19} instead of {name: Beatrice, age: 21}). The two failures are nodeunit deepEqual assertions whose stack frames name only nodeunit internals and test/processor.js; lodash, minBy, maxBy and lib/processor.js never appear.
reference_fix: The reference fix changes the two mappings in lib/processor.js to `min: _.minBy` and `max: _.maxBy`, and additionally changes `_.sample(content, n)` to `_.sampleSize(content, n)` in the same file.
documented_in: The lodash Changelog for v4.0.0 (https://github.com/lodash/lodash/wiki/Changelog), Compatibility Warnings section, states "Split `_.max` & `_.min` into `_.maxBy` & `_.minBy`" and includes a before/after code block (`_.max(objects, 'a')` in 3.10.1 versus `_.maxBy(objects, 'a')` in 4.0.0), which shows the new code form; the `_.sample` to `_.sampleSize` entry in the same section has prose only.
